design:
What the code shows (2026-11-10): two settings-row systems coexist. The newer `SettingsRow` (hub/ui/src/components/ui/settings.tsx; grid in styles/primitives.css, text column `minmax(0,1fr)` beside a 220–300px control column) holds up better. The older `settings-row` (components/environment/SettingsSection.tsx; flex in index.css, stacking only under a narrow-viewport media query) is used by Agent settings, Spec steps, Traces and the Quality panel — and every screen whose label column collapses is on it. Converging on one row behaviour is the expected direction, but which component survives is the builder's call; the requirements state only what must be observable.

"Long values" in this document means: names at their stored maximum (agent 32 characters, check name 64), folder paths of 260 characters, commands of 400 characters, model ids and branch names of 80 characters, and lists of at least five such items.

Where the check runs (readiness review, 2026-11-10): NOT the UI mock. The mock's fixtures (hub/ui/mock/fixtures/*.json) are recorded from the operator's own projects and gitignored, so no builder's checkout has them and the mock does not build there. The check therefore starts its own Hub from the checkout's source on a temporary database and a temporary project folder (deeply nested, so its paths are long), seeds the long values through the Hub's own API (runners, agents, charters, checks, reach grants, generated files, main branch, CI check names), serves the checkout's UI against it (Vite dev server with AW_DEV_HUB, or a local build), and sweeps every section with a headless browser (Python Playwright is installed). It must never point at :8000, and should not use the trial Hub :8010, whose database carries enabled jobs that would fire. The audit's throwaway sweep (testbed/ui-judge/settings-audit/sweep.py) shows the measurement; it is a starting point, not the deliverable.

Environment: task checkouts may lack hub/ui/node_modules (the shared-folder link can fail on this machine); run `npm ci` in hub/ui first when it is missing. That is set-up, not a defect of the work.

problem: The 2026-11-10 audit (roadmap `settings-that-are-easy-to-find-and-match-the-app`) found settings screens that break on long content. Agent settings → Context and Workspace collapse their label column to one word per line at every width and scroll sideways by 157–236px at 1024px; project General's granted-reach paths run off the page; a check with path filters overflows its row, overlaps the next one and hides its edit/move/remove buttons at 1024px; long main branch, CI check names and generated-file commands are cut to one input width; provider-session rows squeeze their label to ~120px; Diagnostics scrolls sideways; worktree paths lose the part that differs; and the project tab bar is clipped at 1024px. Nothing measures this, so it returns whenever a screen is touched.

requirements.rationale: Sideways scroll hides controls entirely; the audit found three sections doing it at 1024px.
requirements.statement: At window widths of 960px and wider, in dark and light mode, no App, Project or Agent settings section scrolls horizontally or places any text or control outside the window, when its values are long values as defined in this document.

requirements.rationale: Agent Context and Workspace showed a description one word per line because the control beside it would not give up width.
requirements.statement: Where a setting's label and description sit beside its control, the text column is at least 240px wide; when the control cannot fit beside text of that width, the control moves below the text and takes the row's width instead.

requirements.rationale: End-truncation hid exactly the part of a worktree path that differs between rows.
requirements.statement: A long value shown read-only (a path, command, id, branch or model id) either wraps or is shortened in the middle keeping its beginning and its last segment, and its full value is shown on hover; a path or id can also be copied whole in one action.

requirements.rationale: Generated files, Main branch and CI check names showed only their first ~30 characters.
requirements.statement: A command or a list of paths or names is edited in a field that shows the whole value, wrapping onto further lines as needed; a single-line field whose value is longer than it can show displays the full value on hover.

requirements.rationale: A check with path filters overlapped the next row and 'Add check', and its edit buttons left the screen.
requirements.statement: Each item in a settings list (checks, granted folders and hosts, provider sessions, worktrees, CI check names, spec steps) grows in height to fit its content; no item overlaps another item or the list's add control, and each item's actions stay visible inside its row at 960px.
Errors, warnings and hints shown under or beside a control wrap within the row and never widen it.

requirements.rationale: At 1024px the bar showed 'Vaul' and no way to Jobs or Activity, so settings at the supported width could not be left for those tabs.
requirements.statement: When the project's tabs do not all fit in the top bar, none is cut mid-word, and the ones that do not fit are reachable from an overflow control in the bar.

requirements.rationale: Nothing measured this, which is how it broke unnoticed; the check is what keeps the slice true. It must not depend on files only one checkout has.
requirements.statement: A repeatable check, runnable from a fresh checkout of the repository on this machine with one command, renders every App, Project and Agent settings section with long values at 960px and 1440px, dark and light, and fails naming the section and the element whenever something scrolls sideways, sits outside the window, or leaves a text column under 240px beside its control.

in_scope: Every App, Project and Agent settings section and the rows, lists, fields and messages inside them
The project tab bar, at the widths where settings are used
A repeatable long-values check over all those sections
non_goals: Restructuring sections, renaming settings, changing save behaviour or restyling — that is slice settings-in-the-apps-style
Rewording messages (e.g. the runner error naming an API route) — slice 2; this slice only makes them fit
Screens outside settings, other than the tab bar
Making the check part of the project's landing checks — it needs a browser and a Hub, and stays a check agents and the operator run

summary: Every settings screen (app, project, agent) stays readable and usable with long paths, commands, names and ids at 960px and wider: no sideways scroll, labels keep a readable width, long values can be read whole, lists grow to fit, and a repeatable check keeps it that way.

tasks.description: In hub/ui/src/index.css the rule `@container (max-width: 447px) { .settings-row-control { flex: 1 1 100%; justify-content: flex-start; min-width: 0 } }` sits before the base `.settings-row-control { display:flex; flex:none; ... justify-content:flex-end }` at equal specificity, so the base rule wins and the container query never takes effect. A control that has wrapped below its text in the older .settings-row therefore keeps its content width and stays right-aligned. Example: Agent → Workspace → Provider sessions at 960px, where the control box is 503–683 and 'No sessions yet.' sits at 599–683, mid-row. Make the wrapped control take the row's width and start at the text's edge: reorder the rules or raise the container rule's specificity. Then rebuild the bundle (npm run build + scripts/refresh_ui_bundle.py) and commit src and bundle together. Ideally the long-values check should also measure that a wrapped control spans the row, so this cannot regress unseen.
tasks.title: Wrapped settings-row control takes the row's width
